evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Applications that use UriComponentsBuilder to parse an externally provided URL and perform validation checks on the host of the parsed URL may be vulnerable to open redirect / SSRF. This is the same as CVE-2024-22259, but with different input. The CVE-2024-22259 fix (6.1.5) made USERINFO accept '@', HOST_IPV4 accept '[', and added checkSchemeAndHost, but left backslash '\' OUT of the excluded character classes of SCHEME/USERINFO/HOST_IPV4/PORT. A browser (WHATWG URL parser) treats '\' as '/' in special (http/https) schemes and ends the authority at the first '\', so a URL 'http://attacker\@allowlisted' still makes getHost() report the allow-listed host while the real navigation target is attacker-controlled.
evidence.distinctness_vs_prior: GENUINELY DISTINCT from CVE-2024-22259. -22259 residual 'http://@trusted.internal[@sidecar.internal' (allow-listed host FIRST, attacker LAST; abuses a leading '@' + '[' HOST_IPV4 truncation). -22262 residual 'http://sidecar.internal\@trusted.internal' (attacker host FIRST, allow-listed host LAST; abuses backslash '\' as a WHATWG special-scheme authority terminator with Spring's last-'@' userinfo binding). Different delimiter ('\' vs '['), different browser mechanism, opposite host ordering. Runtime-confirmed non-dup: on V1=6.1.5 the -22259 seed is BLOCKED (getHost=sidecar.internal) while the -22262 residual PASSES (getHost=trusted.internal).
